title: A cooling failure reveals the common control problem across cloud, AI and cyber
mainJudgement: Dependency risk is only understood when firms can show how physical infrastructure, software, suppliers and automated decisions fail together.

judgement.observation: A cooling failure disrupted several Google Cloud services together while regulators sharpened expectations for agents, cyber exploitation and technology risk.
judgement.executiveJudgement: These are not separate stories. They expose the same weakness: control frameworks often describe services, suppliers and risks independently even when the underlying failure domains are shared. A cloud zone, privileged agent, vulnerable product or outsourced process can connect several important services before governance recognises the concentration.
judgement.implication: Committees should ask for evidence that dependency maps, permissions, patch priorities and recovery tests reflect correlated failure. The useful test is whether the firm can identify what else fails, who can intervene and how service is restored when one supposedly contained dependency breaks.
